title: Complete the preflight C++ keyword list
body:
## Summary
The preflight's C++ keyword list omits reserved words, so such a zone name passes yet will not compile.

## Description
CPP_KEYWORDS in src/lib/level-design/streaming-preflight.ts:56 is a hand-maintained list; a zone named 'register', 'export', 'not' or 'typename' gets no invalid-identifier finding and reaches EWorldZone, despite the module's stated policy that compile-breakers block Generate. Outside this context's file_paths.

## Flow
- Name a zone 'register'
- preflight reports nothing
- EWorldZone gets the reserved word as an enumerator

## Expected impact
Designers with such names stop getting a broken enum; nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every C++ reserved word blocks Generate
Before: 40 of 40 reserved words checked are absent from the 52-entry list (alignas, and, export, register, typename, ...)
After: 0 absent; a table test over the reserved set
Method: simulation - counted the list against the C++20 keyword set; not run because the file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: table-driven vitest of preflight over the C++20 reserved-word set

title: Add undo to the streaming plan
body:
## Summary
Plan edits, including erase that drops linked transitions, have no undo.

## Description
applyStreamingOp in src/lib/level-design/streaming-plan.ts:169 is a pure reducer with no history; erase (:201) removes a zone and every transition touching it in one click. The sibling flow editor already has named-op undo (commit 257578b7).

## Flow
- Erase a zone with 3 links
- all 3 transitions disappear
- no way back but repainting and relinking

## Expected impact
An erase misclick stops costing the links. Reducer history must exclude mode and selection.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one gesture is one undo step
Before: 0 undo steps
After: erase then undo restores zones and transitions
Method: simulation - walked erase, paint and fix ops against the flow editor's model; building it exceeds a Lane A S
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: reducer test: erase + undo deep-equals the prior document

title: Scope the streaming plan to the level document
body:
## Summary
One streaming plan is shared by every level document and is lost on reload.

## Description
useLevelDesignView.ts:134 holds a single useReducer seeded from demo data with no document id and no persistence, so opening another document shows the previous document's zones, and a reload resets to the demo plan.

## Flow
- Paint zones on document A
- open document B
- the same zones are shown as B's plan
- reload: both revert to the demo seed

## Expected impact
Designers stop generating C++ for the wrong level. Needs a storage decision and a migration path for the shape.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a plan belongs to its document and survives reload
Before: 1 plan across N documents, 0 persisted
After: 1 per document, restored after reload
Method: simulation - read the reducer owner; persistence needs a schema not owned by this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: edit under doc A, switch to B, expect the seed; back to A, expect the edit

title: Move the planner's arbitrary-value hex classes to tokens
body:
## Summary
Tailwind arbitrary hex classes bypass the repo's no-hex rule, which only sees string literals in code.

## Description
PaintPalette.tsx:60, PaintPalette.tsx:72, ZoneEditor.tsx:124 and the bg-[#03030a] panels hardcode colours in className; ESLint reports 0 of them, so the no-hex convention is unenforced here.

## Flow
- grep the context for [# class values
- replace each with a chart-colors constant or CSS variable

## Expected impact
Panels follow theme tokens. Purely visual, so a before/after screenshot is the review.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no hex literals in the context
Before: 14 arbitrary hex classes across 7 files
After: 0
Method: probe - grep counted the sites; replacement needs a visual check this round cannot run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the grep count at 0 plus a screenshot of the Streaming tab

title: Name non-adjacent preflight findings and let Escape cancel a mode
body:
## Summary
A non-adjacent link is chipped 'hitch risk' though its message is a missing boundary, and no key cancels paint, erase or link.

## Description
PreflightPanel.tsx chip() labels every warning 'hitch risk', including non-adjacent whose text says the zones share no boundary. Paint, erase and link modes (streaming-plan.ts:181 cancelMode) can only be left via the palette; the grid has no Escape handler.

## Flow
- Draw a seamless link across 3 cells: the chip reads hitch risk
- enter link mode from the keyboard: Escape does nothing

## Expected impact
The chip matches the message and a keyboard user can leave a mode.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - chip names the rule; Escape returns to select
Before: 1 of 2 warning rules mislabelled; 0 keys cancel a mode
After: 2 of 2; Escape dispatches cancelMode
Method: simulation - read chip() and the grid key handler; not built for lack of round budget
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: panel test for the non-adjacent chip and a keyDown Escape test on ZoneGrid
